item.title: New York Builds Data Team to Target Consumer Ripoffs
item.description: [Bloomberg] New York City is building a 36-person bureau of data scientists, technologists and economists to analyze company records for potential violations involving pricing, wages and other consumer and worker protections. NYC Consumer and Worker Protection Commissioner Sam Levine tells David Gura and Christina Ruffini on Bloomberg This Weekend that the effort is designed to give the city the technical expertise to enforce existing laws as algorithms and AI play a growing role in how companies set prices and compensation. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Governor Cox Says Americans Need Healthier Conflict
item.description: [Bloomberg] Utah Governor Spencer Cox joins Bloomberg This Weekend and argues Americans need more substantive disagreement without the contempt he says is fueling polarization, damaged relationships and political violence. In his new book, Off Ramp, Cox calls for healthier political conflict and stronger local connections while also arguing that policymakers need more expertise to address emerging challenges such as AI. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: US Greenland Deal Shifts Focus to Investment
item.description: [Bloomberg] A new security agreement between the US, Denmark and Greenland would expand the American military role while preserving Greenlandic sovereignty, shifting attention toward potential US investment in mining, infrastructure and tourism. Former US diplomat Lewis Lukens tells David Gura and Christina Ruffini on Bloomberg This Weekend that Greenland welcomes investment but faces formidable obstacles including limited transportation infrastructure, a small workforce and the high cost of developing projects in the Arctic. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: UN Talks Offer a New Opening on Iran War
item.description: [Bloomberg] World leaders head to the UN General Assembly as Gulf states seek renewed diplomacy to reduce attacks, restore more predictable energy flows and move the Iran war away from active conflict. Suzanne Maloney of the Brookings Institution joins David Gura and Christina Ruffini on Bloomberg This Weekend and says disruptions to Saudi Arabia’s East-West pipeline and other regional infrastructure are adding urgency to those efforts as Gulf economies face mounting pressure from the conflict. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Can India Turn Its Promise Into Prosperity?
item.description: [Bloomberg] Blackstone COO Jon Gray says India’s young population, expanding middle class and improving infrastructure are drawing interest from global investors. But India’s demographic advantage also creates pressure: millions of young people graduate every year, while formal-sector job creation has not kept pace with their skills and expectations. At the same time, Indian states are competing aggressively for investment by cutting regulatory barriers, building industrial infrastructure and targeting sectors from electronics to semiconductors. The question is whether India can turn its scale, talent and investment momentum into enough productive jobs to sustain its growth. (Source: Bloomberg)
